title: $46B of hard truths from Ben Horowitz: Why founders fail and why you need to run toward fear (a16z co-founder)
summary: Ben Horowitz is the co-founder of Andreessen Horowitz, Silicon Valley’s largest and most influential venture capital firm, with over $46B in committed capital across multiple funds. He took Loudcloud public with just $2 million in revenue (dubbed “the IPO from hell”), sold it for $1.6 billion, and has backed companies from Facebook to Stripe to Airbnb to OpenAI to Databricks (now worth more than $100 billion). His management philosophy—forged through near-death experiences and refined through coaching hundreds of CEOs—contradicts most conventional startup wisdom. In our conversation, Ben shares: 1. Why “founder mode” is half right and half dangerously wrong 2. The story behind “Good Product Manager/Bad Product Manager” and why it went viral despite being written in anger 3. Where the biggest AI startup opportunities remain 4. Why you need to run toward fear, never away 5. The one trait that predicts that a founder will fail as CEO 6.
